_note: Omnisciente practical verification guidance to support assessment of CIS Controls v8.1 IG1 safeguards. Not CIS text and not additional CIS requirements. Cadences are referenced only where the catalog records one. Items flagged stronger go beyond the minimum IG1 safeguard expectation.

foundation.text: An enterprise asset inventory exists
End-user devices, servers, network devices and mobile devices are included
Remote and regularly connected assets outside enterprise control are included
Each asset records an identifier, owner and authorization status

operational.text: New assets are added and retired assets are removed as changes occur
The inventory is reviewed and updated at least every six months
Changes are reconciled against the source used to build the inventory

mature.text: The inventory is compared with an independent source such as discovery or endpoint data
Differences found in that comparison are resolved, not only listed
The most recent review date falls within the six-month cycle

foundation.text: Unauthorized assets can be detected on the network
A defined response exists: remove, deny access or quarantine
Each response option says who can approve an asset instead

operational.text: Unauthorized assets are addressed at least weekly
Each detected asset receives a recorded decision
Quarantined assets stay isolated until a decision is made

mature.text: Recent cases show a decision and a closure date
Assets that reappear after removal are identified
Detection covers remote and wireless connections as well as wired

foundation.text: A software inventory exists for enterprise assets
Entries record title, publisher, version and business purpose
Licensing and ownership information is recorded where applicable

operational.text: Newly authorized software is added to the inventory
Removed or retired software is taken out of the inventory
The inventory is reviewed and updated at least every six months

mature.text: The inventory is compared with software actually installed on assets
Cloud and SaaS applications in use are reflected, not only installed software
Differences between inventory and installed software are resolved

foundation.text: Vendor support status is known for each authorized title
Only currently supported software is designated as authorized
Unsupported software that must remain has a documented exception

operational.text: Support status is checked at least monthly
Titles reaching end of support are removed or given an exception
Each exception records mitigating controls and residual risk acceptance

mature.text: Exceptions are revisited at each monthly review
Exceptions are closed once the software is removed or upgraded
No unsupported title is found on assets without a matching exception

foundation.text: Unauthorized software can be identified on enterprise assets
The response is defined: remove or document an exception
Authorized software is defined clearly enough to tell the difference

operational.text: Unauthorized software is reviewed at least monthly
Each finding is removed or recorded as an exception
Removals are dated so the outcome can be followed

mature.text: Recent findings show resolution, not only detection
Titles that are repeatedly reinstalled are identified
Documented exceptions are revisited rather than left open indefinitely

foundation.text: A data management process is documented
Data sensitivity and data owners are addressed
Handling, retention limits and disposal requirements are covered

operational.text: The process is available to the people who handle enterprise data
The data management process is reviewed and updated annually
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the data management process

mature.text: The process matches how data is actually handled in practice
Retention and disposal statements are consistent with safeguards 3.4 and 3.5
The last review of the data management process falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: A data inventory exists for sensitive data
Each entry records where the data is stored
Data owners or accountable contacts are recorded

operational.text: The inventory is updated when systems that store sensitive data change
The inventory is reviewed and updated at least annually
Sensitive data is prioritized in the inventory

mature.text: Cloud and SaaS repositories that hold sensitive data are included
Sensitive data discovered outside listed locations is added or removed
The last update date falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: Access permissions are configured on sensitive data repositories
Permissions reflect each user's need to know
File shares, databases and cloud storage are covered

operational.text: Permission changes follow the enterprise access approval path
Overly broad permissions are corrected when found
Access is adjusted when a user's role changes

mature.text: Permission exports match the documented access model
Broad groups and external sharing links are identified and justified
Access for users who no longer need it is removed promptly

foundation.text: Retention periods are defined for each data category
Both minimum and maximum retention timelines are stated
Systems holding data subject to retention are identified

operational.text: Retention is applied through system settings or a performed procedure
Data is removed once its maximum retention period has passed
New systems adopt the defined retention periods

mature.text: Retention settings are checked against the documented periods
Records show deletions actually occur at end of retention
Any data kept beyond its period has a documented reason

foundation.text: Disposal methods are defined for enterprise data
Methods are matched to data sensitivity
Physical media and devices are covered as well as electronic data

operational.text: Disposals are recorded when they occur
The disposal method used matches the data's sensitivity
Certificates of destruction are obtained where a third party disposes of media

mature.text: Disposal records identify what was disposed of, how and by whom
Retired assets in the inventory have a matching disposal record
Missing disposal records are followed up

foundation.text: Encryption is enabled on end-user devices that hold sensitive data
Laptops and mobile devices are in scope
The encryption method is identified for each device type

operational.text: New devices are encrypted before they are issued
Devices found unencrypted are encrypted or given a documented exception
Encryption status can be confirmed across in-scope devices

mature.text: Encryption coverage is reconciled with the asset inventory
Remaining unencrypted devices have a documented reason
Recovery keys, where used, are stored so authorized staff can retrieve them

foundation.text: A secure configuration process is documented
It covers end-user devices, servers, non-computing devices and software
Configuration baselines exist for the asset types in use

operational.text: Baselines are applied when assets are built or deployed
Deviations from a baseline are approved and recorded
The secure configuration process is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: Deployed assets are checked against their baseline
Configuration drift found in those checks is corrected
Significant enterprise changes prompt a baseline review

foundation.text: A secure configuration process exists for network devices
Firewalls, routers, switches and wireless equipment are covered
Configuration standards are documented for each device type

operational.text: Network configuration changes follow a recorded change process
Device configurations are backed up
The network configuration process is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: Device configurations are compared against the documented standard
Settings that do not match the standard are corrected or approved
Significant network changes prompt a review of the standards

foundation.text: Automatic session locking is configured on enterprise assets
General-purpose operating systems lock after no more than 15 minutes of inactivity
Mobile devices lock after no more than 2 minutes of inactivity

operational.text: The lock setting is applied by policy rather than left to users
New devices receive the lock setting before use
Devices missing the setting are corrected

mature.text: Lock settings are confirmed on a sample of devices of each type
Devices with a longer timeout have a documented reason
Coverage matches the assets listed in the inventory

foundation.text: A firewall is enabled on servers where supported
The server types in scope are identified
Permitted inbound traffic is defined for each server role

operational.text: Firewall rule changes follow the enterprise change process
Servers found with the firewall disabled are corrected
New servers have the firewall enabled before production use

mature.text: Rules are reviewed and unused rules are removed
Each open port or service has a stated business reason
Firewall coverage matches the servers listed in the inventory

foundation.text: A host firewall is enabled on end-user devices where supported
A default-deny rule drops traffic except permitted services
Permitted exceptions are documented

operational.text: The firewall setting is applied by policy
Devices with the firewall off are corrected
New devices have the firewall enabled before use

mature.text: Firewall status is confirmed across in-scope devices
Standard users cannot turn the firewall off
Exceptions are revisited and removed when no longer needed

foundation.text: Administrative access to assets and software uses secure protocols such as SSH or HTTPS
Insecure management protocols such as Telnet and HTTP are disabled
Version-controlled infrastructure-as-code is protected where used

operational.text: New assets are deployed with secure management settings
Insecure management protocols found in use are disabled
Changes to management configuration follow the change process

mature.text: Management interfaces are checked for insecure protocols
Any remaining insecure protocol has a documented reason
Access to management tooling is limited to administrators

foundation.text: Default accounts are identified on assets and software
Default accounts are disabled, or their passwords are changed
Network devices, applications and cloud services are included

operational.text: New deployments include handling of default accounts
Default account status is checked after installation or reset
Default accounts that must stay enabled are documented

mature.text: A recent check confirms no vendor default credentials remain
Enabled default accounts are limited to those with a stated need
Devices restored to factory settings are rechecked

foundation.text: An inventory of all accounts managed in the enterprise exists
User, administrator and service accounts are included
Entries record name, username, department and start and stop dates

operational.text: The inventory is validated at least quarterly
Validation confirms every active account is authorized
Unauthorized or unknown accounts found are disabled or removed

mature.text: The inventory is reconciled with workforce records
Accounts in cloud and SaaS services are included
The last validation date falls within the quarterly cycle

foundation.text: Unique passwords are required for all enterprise assets
Accounts using MFA require at least an 8-character password
Accounts not using MFA require at least a 14-character password

operational.text: Password requirements are enforced by system settings where supported
Shared credentials are replaced with individual accounts where possible
Users are told not to reuse passwords across accounts

mature.text: Password settings in each identity system are checked against the requirements
Systems that cannot enforce the requirements are identified
Credentials found to be shared or reused are changed

foundation.text: Dormant accounts can be identified from last sign-in data
The inactivity threshold is 45 days where supported
The response is defined: disable or delete

operational.text: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled or deleted where supported
The check is automated or performed as a recorded task
Accounts kept active despite inactivity have an approved reason

mature.text: Recent results show dormant accounts actually disabled
Service and cloud accounts are included in the check
Systems that cannot report inactivity are identified

foundation.text: Administrators have dedicated administrator accounts
Everyday user accounts do not hold administrative privileges
Administrator accounts are not used for email or web browsing

operational.text: New administrative access is granted to dedicated accounts only
Administrative role assignments are limited to administrator accounts
Privileges are removed when administration duties end

mature.text: A current list of privileged accounts is reviewed and justified
Standard accounts found with administrative rights are corrected
Local administrator rights on end-user devices are included in the review

foundation.text: An access granting process is documented
Access is granted on hire and on role change through the process
Access requests are approved before access is provided

operational.text: Recent new hires show approval before access was granted
Role changes follow the same request and approval path
Access granted matches what was approved

mature.text: The process is automated where possible
A sample of recent grants traces back to an approved request
Access granted outside the process is identified and corrected

foundation.text: An access revoking process is documented
Termination, rights revocation and role change all trigger it
Accounts are disabled rather than deleted where audit history must be kept

operational.text: Access is revoked promptly when a trigger occurs
Departures and role changes reach whoever removes the access
Revocations are dated so timeliness can be confirmed

mature.text: Recent leavers show access disabled on or before their last day
SaaS and third-party accounts are included, not only the directory
Late or missed revocations are identified and corrected

foundation.text: Externally exposed enterprise and third-party applications are identified
MFA is required on those applications where supported
Applications that cannot support MFA are identified

operational.text: MFA is enforced by configuration rather than left to user choice
New externally exposed applications require MFA before go-live
Accounts excluded from MFA are identified with a reason

mature.text: MFA coverage is compared with the list of exposed applications
Legacy sign-in methods that bypass MFA are disabled or justified
MFA exclusions are revisited and removed when no longer needed

foundation.text: Remote network access methods are identified
MFA is required for every remote network access method
VPN and remote desktop gateways are included

operational.text: MFA is enforced for all users of remote access
New remote access paths require MFA before use
Remote access attempts without MFA are blocked

mature.text: No remote access path bypasses MFA
Configuration confirms MFA enforcement on each method
Remote access MFA exceptions are revisited and removed when possible

foundation.text: MFA is required for all administrative access where supported
Administrative consoles and cloud administrator roles are included
Accounts managed on-site and by third-party providers are included

operational.text: MFA is enforced by configuration for administrator accounts
New privileged roles require MFA from creation
Administrative sign-ins without MFA are identified

mature.text: MFA coverage is compared with the list of privileged accounts
Emergency access accounts are documented and protected
Administrative MFA exceptions are justified and time-limited

foundation.text: A vulnerability management process is documented
It covers how vulnerabilities are identified for enterprise assets
It defines how findings are prioritized

operational.text: The process is followed for scanning and review
Findings flow into the remediation process in safeguard 7.2
The vulnerability management process is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: The process covers all asset types listed in the inventory
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the vulnerability management process
The last review of the vulnerability management process falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: A risk-based remediation process is documented
Remediation timelines are defined by severity
The process explains how exceptions are handled

operational.text: The remediation process is reviewed at least monthly
Open vulnerabilities are tracked to closure or exception
Findings are prioritized by risk

mature.text: Remediation is completed within the defined timelines
Overdue remediation is escalated
Accepted risks are revisited rather than left open indefinitely

foundation.text: Operating system updates are automated on enterprise assets
Workstations and servers are covered
The update schedule is defined

operational.text: Operating system updates are applied at least monthly
Failed update installations are identified
Devices missing updates are remediated

mature.text: Update status is compared with the asset inventory
Devices excluded from automated updates have a documented reason
Devices that repeatedly fail to update are investigated

foundation.text: Application updates are automated on enterprise assets
Commonly used third-party applications are in scope
Applications that cannot be updated automatically are identified

operational.text: Application updates are applied at least monthly
Failed application updates are identified
Outdated applications are updated or removed

mature.text: Update status is compared with the software inventory
Applications excluded from automated updates have a documented reason
Applications with no available update are handled under safeguard 2.2

foundation.text: An audit log management process is documented
It defines which logs are collected
It defines log review and retention requirements

operational.text: New systems are brought into log collection under the process
The audit log management process is reviewed and updated annually
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the audit log management process

mature.text: Collection in practice matches the documented process
Retention requirements are consistent with safeguard 8.3
The last review of the audit log management process falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: Audit logging is enabled on enterprise assets
Identity, endpoint and key systems are included
Logged events match the audit log management process

operational.text: New assets are configured to produce audit logs
Gaps in log collection are identified
Log sources that stop producing logs are corrected

mature.text: A sample confirms logs are actually being generated
Log source coverage is compared with the asset inventory
Missing log sources are tracked until resolved

foundation.text: Audit log storage is sized for the defined retention needs
The storage location for audit logs is defined
Retention settings are configured

operational.text: Log storage use is monitored
Storage shortfalls are addressed before logs are lost
Storage is reassessed when log volume changes

mature.text: Retention settings are confirmed against the logging process
Stored logs cover the full defined retention period
Any log loss is identified and explained

foundation.text: Approved browsers and email clients are defined
Only fully supported browsers and email clients are allowed
Automatic updates are enabled where supported

operational.text: Supported versions are kept current as vendors release updates
Unsupported versions are identified
Outdated clients are updated or removed

mature.text: Browser and email client versions are listed across devices
No unsupported version remains without a documented reason
Unapproved browsers or email clients are removed

foundation.text: DNS filtering is in use on enterprise assets
Known malicious domains are blocked
Remote and off-network devices are included

operational.text: New devices receive DNS filtering before use
Devices that bypass DNS filtering are corrected
Filtering exceptions are recorded

mature.text: DNS filtering coverage is compared with the asset inventory
Filtering is confirmed on devices away from the office network
Filtering exceptions are revisited and removed when no longer needed

foundation.text: Anti-malware software is deployed on enterprise assets
Servers and end-user devices are included
Anti-malware software is kept maintained and current

operational.text: New assets receive anti-malware before use
Assets without working anti-malware are identified
Missing or inactive agents are corrected

mature.text: Anti-malware coverage is reconciled with the asset inventory
Devices unable to run anti-malware have a documented reason
Agents that stop reporting are investigated

foundation.text: Automatic signature updates are enabled for anti-malware
Updates apply to all assets running anti-malware
Update failures are visible

operational.text: Assets with out-of-date signatures are identified
Out-of-date signatures are corrected
New assets receive automatic updates

mature.text: Signature currency is confirmed across assets
Assets that repeatedly fail to update are investigated
Offline or rarely connected devices are included

foundation.text: Autorun is disabled for removable media
Autoplay is disabled for removable media
The setting covers all operating systems in use where supported

operational.text: The setting is applied by policy
New devices receive the setting before use
Devices missing the setting are corrected

mature.text: The setting is confirmed on a sample of devices
Devices without the setting have a documented reason
Coverage matches the devices listed in the inventory

foundation.text: A data recovery process is documented
Recovery scope and priorities are defined
Backup procedures and protection of recovery data are covered

operational.text: New systems are brought into the recovery process
The data recovery process is reviewed and updated annually
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the data recovery process

mature.text: Recovery priorities match the systems the enterprise depends on
The process is consistent with safeguards 11.2 to 11.4
The last review of the data recovery process falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: Automated backups are configured for in-scope enterprise assets
Backups run at least weekly, more often for sensitive data
The systems and data in backup scope are identified

operational.text: Backup job results are checked
Failed backups are investigated and rerun
New in-scope systems are added to backups

mature.text: Backup coverage is compared with the in-scope systems
Cloud and SaaS data in scope is backed up
A test restore shows backups can be recovered

foundation.text: Recovery data is protected with access controls
Protection is equivalent to the original data's sensitivity
Encryption or separation is used where the data requires it

operational.text: Access to backup systems is limited to those who need it
Changes to backup access follow the access approval path
Backup credentials are separate from everyday accounts

mature.text: Backup access is reviewed and unneeded access is removed
Protection settings are confirmed in configuration
Deleting backups requires elevated rights or is prevented

foundation.text: An isolated instance of recovery data exists
Isolation is achieved by offline storage, cloud separation or immutability
The isolated copy includes the data needed for recovery

operational.text: The isolated copy is kept up to date
Primary-system credentials cannot alter or delete the isolated copy
Isolated copy status is checked

mature.text: Isolation is confirmed in configuration, not assumed
A restore from the isolated copy shows it can be recovered
Changes to backup architecture preserve the isolation

foundation.text: Network infrastructure is identified
Firmware and software versions are known for each device
Devices run vendor-supported versions

operational.text: Network updates are reviewed at least monthly
Available updates are applied or deferred with a reason
End-of-life devices are identified

mature.text: Versions are compared with vendor support information
End-of-life devices have a replacement or exception decision
Deferred updates are revisited at the next monthly review

foundation.text: A security awareness program exists
Training is provided at hire
Training is provided at least annually thereafter

operational.text: Training completion is tracked
Incomplete training is followed up
Content is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: Completion records cover the whole workforce
Significant enterprise changes prompt a content review
The last content review falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: Training covers recognizing social engineering attacks
Phishing, business email compromise, pretexting and tailgating are included
Workforce members know what to do with a suspicious request

operational.text: Social engineering training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of social engineering training is tracked
Content reflects attack types the enterprise encounters

mature.text: Social engineering training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is refreshed when attack methods change
Phishing exercises, where used, inform the next training update

foundation.text: Training covers authentication best practices
MFA use is explained
Password composition and credential management are covered

operational.text: Authentication training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of authentication training is tracked
Content is consistent with enterprise password and MFA settings

mature.text: Authentication training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is updated when authentication settings change
Credential-related incidents are reflected in later training

foundation.text: Training covers identifying and securely storing sensitive data
Transferring, archiving and destroying sensitive data are covered
Clear-screen and clear-desk practices are included

operational.text: Data handling training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of data handling training is tracked
Content is consistent with the data management process in 3.1

mature.text: Data handling training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is updated when the data management process changes
Data handling incidents are reflected in later training

foundation.text: Training covers causes of unintentional data exposure
Mis-delivery of sensitive data is covered
Lost devices and unintended publication are covered

operational.text: Exposure training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of exposure training is tracked
Examples reflect the tools the workforce actually uses

mature.text: Data exposure training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is updated after exposure-related incidents
Content is reviewed alongside the annual program review

foundation.text: Training covers recognizing a potential incident
Training explains how to report an incident
Examples of reportable events are given

operational.text: Incident reporting training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of incident reporting training is tracked
The reporting channel taught matches the process in 17.3

mature.text: Incident reporting training completion covers the whole workforce
Reporting instructions are updated when contacts or channels change
Incidents reported by workforce members inform later training

foundation.text: Training covers checking whether devices are missing security updates
Training explains how to report a device missing updates
The reporting path for update problems is defined

operational.text: Update awareness training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of update awareness training is tracked
Reported update problems are routed to whoever maintains the devices

mature.text: Update awareness training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is updated when update methods change
Reported update problems are followed through to resolution

foundation.text: Training covers the dangers of insecure networks
Public and home networks are addressed
Expectations for connecting securely are explained

operational.text: Insecure network training is delivered through the awareness program
Completion of insecure network training is tracked
Guidance names the approved way to connect remotely

mature.text: Insecure network training completion covers the whole workforce
Content is updated when remote working arrangements change
Remote workers handling enterprise data are included

foundation.text: An inventory of service providers exists
Each provider has a classification
An enterprise contact is designated for each provider

operational.text: New providers are added at onboarding
Providers that are no longer used are removed
The inventory is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: The inventory is compared with contracts or purchasing records
Providers handling sensitive data are identified
Providers found in use but missing from the inventory are added

foundation.text: A person is designated to manage incident handling
A backup is designated for when the primary is unavailable
Third-party incident handling roles are identified where used

operational.text: Designations are known to the people who need them
Designations are updated when personnel change
Designations are reviewed annually

mature.text: Designated personnel understand their responsibilities
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the designations
The last review of the incident handling designations falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: Contact information exists for reporting security incidents
Internal staff, service providers and relevant authorities are included
Insurers and law enforcement contacts are included where relevant

operational.text: Contact details are verified at least annually
Contact changes are recorded when they occur
The contact list is accessible during an outage

mature.text: Contacts are confirmed as reachable, not only listed
Contacts that are out of date are corrected
The last verification date falls within the annual cycle

foundation.text: An enterprise process for reporting incidents is documented
Reporting timeframes are defined
Personnel to report to and the reporting mechanism are named
The minimum information to report is specified

operational.text: The process is available to the whole workforce
Reported incidents follow the documented process
The incident reporting process is reviewed and updated annually

mature.text: The process is consistent with the contacts in 17.2 and training in 14.6
Significant enterprise changes prompt a review of the incident reporting process
The last review of the incident reporting process falls within the annual cycle
